constructionSite.note: A bounded July 1835 worksite, not a reconstruction of the completed hotel. The 10 June Chicago Democrat notice establishes a house building in Kinzie's Addition, understood to be named Lake House. No source measures the July progress. Within the existing 24 × 15 m plan and 4 m maximum, 0.46 m thick brick walls now step down from the higher north working front to the lower rear lift. Seven selected work bays have real unglazed openings and only the first three have their brickwork bridged above reconstructed timber lintels; a broad rear break admits material. Two short timber working stages stand inside the shell. Bay count, wall thickness, lift heights, apertures, staging stock and placement are reconstructed working choices, not features traced from the later print. The existing external brick, timber and footing-stone piles remain separately declared in the yard layer. No excavation or below-grade interior is represented. L-lake-house-worksite-2379.

libertyRead.text: finish a bounded July worksite, without backdating the later hotel Decision Lake House (under construction) uses the default-off construction site builder: thick, open brick walls with uneven lifts, seven selected work bays, only three bridged openings supported by reconstructed timber lintels, a broad rear material-access break and two interior timber working stages. All pieces stay within the existing 24 × 15 m footprint and four-metre maximum. The existing nine external material piles stay on their independently declared yard layer. Evidence and bounds The held Chicago Democrat 10 June 1835 p.2 col.5 notice attests an active project before 1 July, not its measured progress; the reading is transcription-mediated, with bracketed supplies, and no original facsimile was newly read. Andreas's later completed brick hotel, three storeys and a basement, and autumn 1836 opening bound a substantial unfinished project. The exact July lift is a chosen reconstruction within the retained zero-to-two-storey range. The 0.46 m masonry, chosen seven-bay rhythm, individual apertures, incomplete lintels, lower lifts and 1.65 m stage decks/stock/positions are all invented within those bounds. No source counts or measures them. No cellar excavation, below-grade interior, accommodation or completed-hotel roof/cupola/glazing/sign is represented. The prior position and its uncertainty are retained; no later address or retrospective print relocates it. Picture scope The original Chicago picture is the 1856 Kellogg/Blanchard print, showing the completed ca.1836–1849 hotel. Its planning copy is byte-identical. All four Lake House illustrations embedded in the live Chicagology source page were also read: the about-1860 completed-hotel photograph, the 1869 mapped hotel and two later text-ad/menu composites. None depicts July progress; no asset is derived from that check required site. The 1869 map places the later hotel west of Rush, contradicting the existing reconstructed east-side choice; that later-state conflict is recorded without tracing it into July coordinates. Milwaukee's Lake House is a different building. The completed print remains credited later context and is ineligible to prescribe July construction progress. No empty matches verdict is created. Any image-gate exception for the original piece of work must name this wrong-date ruling. A measured contemporary plan or dated progress picture could replace the reconstruction; missing exact numbers do not block building it at this row. Sources The Chicago Democrat. Vol. I, No. 1 (November 26, 1833) through Vol. II, No. 18…, Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the Earliest Period to the Present Time.
